> board's height in its file and in `canvas.json`). The Figma re-sync steps below are kept as history.


This folder keeps what is needed to re-sync two Claude artifacts with the Figma file "JusPrin v2"
(file key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`), and to prove a re-sync breaks nothing.

- Canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
- JusPrin Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL

It lives outside the JusPrin repo on purpose: it is not product code, and untracked files in the repo mean
"unfinished work" there.

## What is here

- `published/` — an exact copy of what is published now (`canvas/project`, `ds/project`). Every re-sync is
  compared against it, then it is replaced by the new build.
- `figma/spec3/<page id>.txt` — the Figma pages as last read (one text line per layer). `figma/vars.json` —
  Figma's variables, text styles and shadows as last read.
- `tools/` — the scripts (below).
- `visual/figma/*.png` — Figma's own screenshot of each page, used to score the artboards.
  `visual/scores-*.json` — the scores before and after the 2026-10-13 re-import.
- `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` — the published files, the Figma reads and the scripts as they were
  before the re-import of 2026-10-13. Running those scripts on those reads reproduces those files byte for byte.

## Re-sync, step by step

1. Read Figma. For each page id (`0:1 1423:396 320:1053 160:59 9:153 359:116 1148:1287 1258:396 1328:2780`)
   call the Figma tool `use_figma` with the text of `tools/spec3_min.js`, replacing `__PAGE__` and `__OFFSET__`
   (0, then 20200, 40400, ... while the offset is below the returned `total`). About 35 calls; have background
   agents make them, because each reply is large. Run `tools/vars.js` once the same way and save its result as
   `figma/vars.json`. The script source is `tools/figma_spec3.js`; `python3 tools/minify.py tools/figma_spec3.js
   tools/spec3_min.js` rebuilds the one-line version.
2. Decode the replies from the session transcripts:
   `SESSION=<session id> OUT=figma python3 tools/collect.py`
3. Build into a scratch folder `new/`:

       export FIGMA_DIR=$PWD/figma DS_DIR=$PWD/new/ds REPO=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin
       rm -rf new && mkdir new && cp -R published/ds new/ds
       python3 tools/build_variants.py $REPO new/ds
       python3 tools/build_canvas.py $REPO new/canvas <design system version id>
       mkdir -p new/specs/project/screens && cp published/ds/project/tokens.json new/specs/project/
       python3 tools/specs.py $REPO figma/spec3 new/specs/project/screens

4. Compare with what is published: `python3 tools/compare_builds.py published new`. With no change in Figma and
   no change in the scripts, every line must say "identical". Explain every file that is not before publishing.
5. Compare with Figma itself: take a screenshot of each Figma page (`get_screenshot`, maxDimension 8000) into
   `visual/figma/`, then `tools/visual_pages.py`, screenshot each `composite-<page>.html` at full page size,
   and `tools/visual_compare.py`. No artboard may score worse than in `visual/scores-after.json`.
6. Publish only the changed files to the same artifact URLs, check the live pages, then replace `published/`.

content.text:
Both design artifacts now match the filament step Kenneth approved. On the JusPrin v2 canvas (version 38), the old step-3 boards are redrawn as the default state, with 12 new state boards. In the Design System (version 29), MenuRow gains an optional second line of detail. Before editing I backed up the live files to `figma-mirror/live-2026-10-20-filament/`.

**Canvas, "Printer & Material Settings" page:**
- **Step-3 pair:** `printer-prepare-first-print-{light,dark}-add-printer-step-3` now draws the default state. That replaces "What spool is on it right now?" and the made-up "Common on the MK4" list.
- **New boards:** six states in light and dark, as two rows under the existing screens with the title "Add a printer · step 3 · filament states". The states are searching, nothing for this printer, made for other printers shown, your filaments, nothing found anywhere, and creating a preset. Each file is named `…-add-printer-step-3-<state>`.
- **Wording:** it follows the implementation in the add-printer-popup worktree, including "Start with Prusa Generic PLA instead" and the heading "EVERY FILAMENT FOR THE MK4 · 212". I used the warning triangle icon, as the code does.
- **Menu/Row board:** it gains three detail variants. Because the board got taller, the 16 Design System page boards below it moved down 214px to avoid overlapping.
- **Component code:** the canvas's own copy of the component code under `project/ds/jusprin/components/` is updated to match the Design System.

**Design System, MenuRow:**
- **New options:**
  - `detail`: a second line in small secondary text.
  - `detailTone: 'warning'`: a warning triangle before the detail, which then uses primary text.
  - `meta`: short text at the right end of the row, such as the material.
- **Approval scope:** Kenneth approved the second line. `meta` is the "PLA" shown on the right of each row in the prototype he approved, so I added it to the component too.
- **Where it changed:** the README, the preview card (now 9 variants in light and dark, plus a coded filament example), `bundle.js`, `bundle.css` and `index.d.ts`.
- **Spec files:** the 7 light boards have layer-by-layer spec files, and `screens/index.json` and `screens.md` are updated (Printer & Material Settings now lists 27 screens).

**Checks:** I rendered all 14 step-3 boards and the Menu/Row board with headless Chrome and looked at them in both themes, and the edited component code passes a syntax check. I couldn't view the coded preview inside the Design System page itself.

**One finding for the implementation:** the MK4 profile suggests 10 filaments, so in a list 324px tall the "Every filament for the MK4 · 212" heading falls below the visible area. A person sees only suggestions until they scroll, which weakens the "you can see there's more" point of the design. The default board shows this as it really looks. Kenneth may want fewer suggestions shown, or a taller list.

**Still open:** Kenneth asked me to check whether upstream OrcaSlicer lets you pick any filament preset. I paused before launching OrcaSlicer and asked him how he wants it tested; he hasn't answered yet.

The tools are in `figma-mirror/tools/composer/` (`build_filament_step.py` and `measure_sheets.py`). The details are in `filament-step-design-findings.md` in the shared notes folder.

content.text:
No, the checkbox isn't wrong. It covers only the filaments OrcaSlicer itself refuses for this printer, which is the gap you asked to make reachable. Generic and other-brand filaments that OrcaSlicer allows are already in the main list above the checkbox.

For the Anycubic 4Max Pro 2 in your screenshot, I counted from the profiles:
- **About 293 filaments fit**, including Generic PLA, eSUN, Polymaker and Bambu. That is the "Every filament for the 4Max Pro 2" list, and it is what OrcaSlicer's own list would offer once those filaments are installed.
- **32 don't fit**, which matches the "32 more" in your screenshot. Almost all are Anycubic's own profiles, and each one names only newer Anycubic printers. For example, Anycubic PLA is only for the Kobra 2 Max, Neo, Plus and Pro, and Anycubic PETG is only for the Kobra 3 and Kobra S1 models. OrcaSlicer shows these greyed out and won't let you pick them.

I've moved the "Not in the list?" controls out of the scrolling list and replaced "OrcaSlicer" with "JusPrin" in the filament step's text. Both changes are on the JusPrin v2 canvas (version 39) and in the Design System's spec files (version 31). I've sent both to [Build the 3-step manual Add printer popup](#local_f9008dea-bfb7-4930-a952-b66276ec68b2) so it can change the form's code. The JusPrin copy you're testing will show them only after that session rebuilds and you relaunch it.

**New layout, top to bottom:**
- Search field.
- The scrolling list: only filament rows, plus the "No filament … matches" messages when a search finds nothing.
- **A footer that stays in view, outside the scrolling:** "Not in the list?", the "Show filaments made for other printers" checkbox, and "+ Create a filament preset…".
- Skip link, then Back and Cancel.

The checkbox's second line changes with the search: "17 more…" with no search, "2 of them match your search…" when some match, and "None of the 17 match your search either" when none do.

The long sentence "These are all the filaments OrcaSlicer has profiles for…" is gone. The step's text now reads:
- "JusPrin makes filament presets for printers that are already set up, so the MK4 is added first. Then the Create filament window opens…"
- "…for the MK4 or any other printer JusPrin has profiles for."

**"OrcaSlicer" elsewhere:**
- **Fixed on the canvas only:** the conversation board's file-notes card now says "JusPrin said more than fits here." The code (`FileNotesCard.tsx:50`) still says "OrcaSlicer…".
- **The AI agent says it to people:** the printer and filament instructions tell it to call stock presets "the settings OrcaSlicer comes with" (`printerInstructions.ts:197`, `filamentInstructions.ts:42` and `:59`).
- **Only the AI agent reads it:** about 70 error messages from the workspace tools start "OrcaSlicer did not…". The agent's standing instructions already tell it that "OrcaSlicer" in these means JusPrin.
- **Correct as it is:** the onboarding boards' "Bring your Orca setup" and "Orca import" mean importing from a separately installed OrcaSlicer app.

Do you want the first two fixed, the file-notes card and the agent's "the settings OrcaSlicer comes with"? The card is a one-line code change. The agent wording is a change to its instructions, so it could change how the agent phrases things elsewhere, and checking that would need the live-model tests your budget rule makes you approve first. My recommendation: fix the card now, and change the agent's phrase to "the settings JusPrin comes with" together with your next approved prompt test. The tool errors can stay.
